meta.title: Will the Rally in Bitcoin Move to New Highs in 2027?
meta.thread_line: 4 threads · Dow theory breakout and targets · disbelief as fuel · divergence entries · bullish, but no all-time-high timetable

snapshot: Bitcoin broke above its spring and May highs, triggering a **Dow theory** bull signal — Manuel Blay says Bitcoin has bottomed.
Key resistance cleared: $67,264-70,512 and the 200-day SMA; next zone is the $80,600-83,700 retest of major resistance.
Sentiment reads as disbelief: about half of Alessio's commenters expect a retest of the $57-60K summer lows — a contrarian positive.
Both see positive MACD divergences (daily and weekly) at the lows; Charlie turned bullish on the double bottom at the monthly 50 moving average.
Charlie, a long-term unleveraged holder, calls the summer low a major low but won't commit to new all-time highs this year or even next.
Neither knows whether this is a new uptrend or a correction inside the bear market — "nobody can be certain."

themes.status: BREAKOUT — ABOVE SPRING AND MAY HIGHS
themes.title: Bitcoin's Dow theory buy signal and the road to $80-84K
themes.lead: Clearing the spring and May highs flipped the Dow theory model bullish, with the next technical targets in the low 80Ks.
bullets: Taking out the spring and May highs triggered a Dow theory bull signal; trader **Manuel Blay** reads it as Bitcoin having bottomed.
At $60K the same Dow theory model pointed to the bear market extending to $50K — Alessio admits he was leaning that way too.
Confirmation level: an impulsive break above $67,264-70,512 resistance, now achieved along with the 200-day SMA.
Alessio's August 20 member video flagged a rally to $77K and even $82K once the trend line broke.
If support holds, the higher-probability path is the 138.2% and 161.8% (golden ratio) extensions; beyond that, a $80,600-83,700 retest at the 38.2% level.

quote.text: One thing we can obviously never be certain of is whether the rally is corrective... or whether the rally is the start of a new uptrend.

themes.watch: Both hosts say they can't tell whether this is a new uptrend or a temporary correction before the bear market resumes.

names.name: Bitcoin (BTC)
names.blurb: Alessio: Dow theory bull signal, probabilities lean to at least an intermediate bottom; targets $80.6-83.7K.

themes.title: Half the crowd still expects $57K — that disbelief is the bull case
themes.lead: Crowd pessimism is a contrarian signal, and this year's Bitcoin mood has been heavily bearish.
bullets: Alessio's comment section splits about 50/50: half expect a retest of the $57-60K lows, half call new all-time highs "obvious."
His overall read: the majority show **disbelief** — supportive of more upside over the next several weeks and months.
Charlie: when Bitcoin hit the $50-odd thousands, many were calling for $30-40K or lower.
Pessimism alone can't be timed — Charlie pairs it with technicals; mixed sentiment now is "healthy for the continuation."
Reading recommendation: Gustave Le Bon's *The Crowd* (1890s) on herd psychology as a contrarian tool.

quote.text: You had negative sentiment. You've got bullish divergences into key levels. That's about all you need.

themes.watch: The sentiment gauge is Alessio's own YouTube comment section, not a market-wide survey.

themes.title: Divergences at the lows: the aggressive entry vs. waiting for the break
themes.lead: Both saw bullish MACD divergences at the lows; they differ only on how early to act on them.
bullets: Daily: Bitcoin made a lower low while MACD made a higher low — a positive divergence.
Weekly: another positive divergence relative to the February low, clearer on the weekly MACD.
Charlie got bullish on the double bottom, which landed on the monthly 50-period moving average.
The summer drop held a major uptrend line, bounced and reclaimed the 200-week average.

Alessio waited for a trend-line break to raise confidence; Charlie, "an aggressive trader," enters once the divergence prints plus one half-decent up-closing bar, with a stop for a better risk-to-reward.

themes.title: A major low is in, but new all-time highs may wait past 2027
themes.lead: Charlie is bullish and holding, yet won't put a date on a return to the $120K-area highs.
bullets: Charlie doesn't trade Bitcoin; he's a long-term, unleveraged investor in it.
The low a few months ago — high-time-frame support plus a flush of negative sentiment — "should be a major low."
Not necessarily new all-time highs this year, "maybe not even next year"; enough scope for a good run even short of $120K.
He won't forecast $150K-200K, and dismisses the $500K-to-$1M callers.
Alessio: if Bitcoin goes back above $100K in the next few months, the "$500K, it's obvious" crowd will reappear.
Same pattern in silver: viewers told Charlie at the start of this year that silver was going to $500.

quote.text: There are fundamental reasons why it could go a lot higher over the longer term. The timing of that I find a bit more difficult.

themes.watch: Charlie says he's "not in the prediction business" — the bullish view carries no timeline.

takeaways.title: Treat $67-70K as the line: holding above it keeps the $80.6-83.7K retest in play.
Gauge crowd mood alongside the chart — widespread disbelief near a breakout is a tailwind, not a warning.
Pick your trigger in advance: divergence plus an up-closing bar (aggressive) or a confirmed trend-line break (conservative).
Size Bitcoin for a long hold without assuming new all-time highs before 2027 ends.

hot_takes.take: My contention is that the low that we put in a few months ago... should be a major low.
I'm not necessarily looking for new all-time highs this year. Maybe not even next year.
If Bitcoin at some point in the next few months goes to 100K and above 100K, I'll guarantee there'll be people out there saying, 'Oh, 500K, it's obvious.'

claims.claim: Bitcoin has bottomed and is in a Dow theory bull market.
Bitcoin can extend to retest major resistance at $80,600-83,700.
claims.condition: as long as Bitcoin holds support above the 200 SMA

claims.claim: The summer low near $57-60K is a major low.
Bitcoin may not make new all-time highs in 2026 or even 2027.

other_news.title: Sources referenced: trader Manuel Blay's Dow theory model and Gustave Le Bon's *The Crowd*.

glossary.def: Trend model that signals a bull market when price breaks above prior swing highs after a decline.
Price makes a lower low while an oscillator like MACD makes a higher low, hinting that selling is fading.
Moving-average convergence divergence, a momentum indicator built from two exponential moving averages.
Fibonacci targets (138.2%, 161.8%) projecting how far a breakout may run.
200-period simple moving average, a common long-term trend line.
Two lows at roughly the same level, read as a potential reversal.
